hints.content: The arrow points to all values greater than $-5$.
And the point at $-5$ is *not* filled in.
So, the inequality represents everything strictly **greater than $-5$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**

[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at negative 5. A line running to the right starts at negative 5 and continues.

choices.clue:
The graph of $x < -5$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at negative 5. A line running to the left starts at negative 5 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/a28ec4cdbcae857b221e01ef395c4ba3cc872fd8)

The graph of $x \leq -5$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A closed point is plotted at negative 5. A line running to the left starts at negative 5 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/18826a96c2941e7d8bcf8b685ba4529deeae05e3)

The graph of $x \geq -5$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 5 to 5 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. A closed point is plotted at negative 5. A line running to the right starts at negative 5 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/69874f535e916761d6944e677f05563855764d53)
